A_target.statement:
Let $\map S {n, k}$ be the number of partitions of an $n$-set into $k$ non-empty blocks.
Then:
:$\map S {n + 1, k} = k \, \map S {n, k} + \map S {n, k - 1}$

B_source.statement: [[Pascal's Rule]] $\dbinom {n + 1} k = \dbinom n k + \dbinom n {k - 1}$ holds since the $k$-subsets of $\set {1, \ldots, n + 1}$ split according to whether they contain $n + 1$.

substitutions.containing n + 1: n + 1 forming a block on its own

derived.the two cases: the two terms of the recurrence

object_map.reformulation: Reuse the case split on the last element from Pascal's rule; the non-singleton case acquires a multiplicity, the choice of block.

validity_conditions: Removing n + 1 from a non-singleton block leaves a partition with the same number of blocks.
Each partition of {1, ..., n} into k blocks extends in exactly k ways.
proof_plan: Split the partitions of $\set {1, \ldots, n + 1}$ into $k$ blocks according to whether $\set {n + 1}$ is a block.
If it is, removing it leaves a partition of $\set {1, \ldots, n}$ into $k - 1$ blocks, giving $\map S {n, k - 1}$ partitions.

If not, removing $n + 1$ leaves a partition of $\set {1, \ldots, n}$ into $k$ blocks.
Conversely each such partition arises from $k$ choices of the block receiving $n + 1$, giving $k \, \map S {n, k}$.

Adding the cases gives the recurrence for [[Definition:Stirling Numbers of the Second Kind|Stirling numbers of the second kind]].
{{qed}}
